request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Narrowing the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian list surfaces accept an optional specialty name and bring back only the veterinarians holding it. The name matches in full, letter case is disregarded, and paging keeps the narrowing. No name, or a blank one, lists everyone as before.
acceptance_criteria: Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the directory page is opened for it, then only those veterinarians are listed and paging applies to that narrowed list.
Given a specialty name differing from the held specialty only by letter case, when either surface is asked for it, then it matches.
Given only part of a specialty's name, when either surface is asked for it, then no veterinarian comes back — the whole name must match.

Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either surface is asked for it, then the page or the machine-readable document comes back normally with an empty veterinarian list and no failure reported.
Given no specialty named, or one that is empty or entirely blank space, when either surface is opened, then it behaves exactly as it does today and lists every veterinarian.
Given a narrowed directory spanning more than one page, when the reader follows a paging link, then the next page is still narrowed to the same specialty.
Given a specialty, when the machine-readable list is asked for it, then it carries every veterinarian holding that specialty and no other.
Blank space around a non-blank specialty name is not disregarded, so a padded name matches nothing; this is the narrowest reading and is recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md.
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or any other page control for choosing the specialty — the narrowing is addressable only
free-text search over veterinarian names, which NG-9 still declines
narrowing either surface by any attribute other than specialty
reviving REQ-VET-002 or reusing its id
notes: Scope decisions taken by the narrowest reading, because the owner states no further product answer will come; each is recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md rather than raised as a consultation. (1) One fresh requirement, REQ-VET-003, carries the narrowing on both surfaces — the owner asked for a fresh requirement, singular, so REQ-VET-001 is left unamended. (2) A name matching no specialty at all is not told apart from one whose specialty no veterinarian holds; both list nothing. (3) Blank space around a non-blank name is not disregarded. Two rows in docs/system-design.md are now stale and are the system-design-expert's to correct: the known-issue row saying the machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement, and open question 5's premise. docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for docs/adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md; that file is outside this agent's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The narrowing extends the existing vet feature package with no new type, package, or dependency: a derived VetRepository query plus an optional request parameter on VetController's two existing routes. Both fit the Repository and Web controller rows of the pattern catalog. The genuinely new ground is the caching boundary — request-supplied text reaching a cache with no size limit, expiry, or eviction — now settled by docs/adr/2026-08-15-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-query.md and recorded as a rule in docs/system-design.md section Caching. Basis for the covering-code claims: grep and direct reads over src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet plus the system-design Contracts table. The IntelliJ oracle is not connected in this run, so this is the weaker grep basis rather than a symbol resolution.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived queries against the specialties association: a Page-returning one taking a Pageable for the HTML route, and a Collection-returning one for the machine-readable route. Neither carries @Cacheable.

VetController.showVetList and showResourcesVetList each gain an optional specialty request parameter. A blank value selects the existing unfiltered repository call, so today's behavior is unchanged when the parameter is absent.
vetList.html pagination links carry the specialty forward. Both surfaces stay GET-only and no new route appears.
The narrowing publishes nothing the directory does not already print beside every veterinarian, so the exposed surface does not widen.

patterns.description: derived paged query taking a Pageable second argument - the shape the narrowed HTML query follows
controller normalizes a blank search term, then delegates - the precedent for the blank-specialty branch
@DataJpaTest against seeded H2 - the established home for a vet repository query test
what may be keyed into the vets cache, with the ADR back-link

risks.risk: VetControllerTests mocks VetRepository, so whole-name matching, case-insensitivity, and the partial-name rejection cannot be verified there. Passing controller tests would assert only that the controller called a mock.
risks.mitigation: Verify the matching acceptance criteria in a @DataJpaTest against seeded H2, beside ClinicServiceTests.shouldFindVets. Leave VetControllerTests to cover surface wiring, blank handling, empty results, and the paging-link carry.

risks.risk: The current pagination hrefs in vetList.html are string-concatenated URLs with Thymeleaf preprocessing. Appending a request-derived specialty the same way emits it unencoded, breaking on & or # and teaching a bad pattern in a sample application.
risks.mitigation: Build the links as Thymeleaf link expressions with named parameters, for example @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encode each parameter. Any visible echo of the value relies on Thymeleaf's default output escaping, which stays on.

risks.risk: The predicate joins the eager @ManyToMany specialties collection. A join that matched more than one row per veterinarian would duplicate content rows and inflate the Page count.
risks.mitigation: A veterinarian links a given specialty once, so duplication is not expected. Assert the element count in the @DataJpaTest; add Distinct to the derived query name if duplicates appear.

risks.risk: Caching the narrowed query under vets would let an unauthenticated caller mint one entry per distinct specialty string against a cache with no eviction or size limit.
risks.mitigation: Ruled out by docs/adr/2026-08-15-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-query.md. The narrowed methods carry no @Cacheable; the unfiltered ones keep theirs unchanged.

risks.risk: Spring Data could fail to resolve the derived name if the nested property path is ambiguous.
risks.mitigation: findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase resolves against Vet.specialties and NamedEntity.name today. The explicit findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase form disambiguates if resolution fails.

notes: Trust boundary and control, per architecture-principles.md Design Principle 1: the boundary is the specialty query parameter on both GET routes. Controls are (a) the derived query, so no request text is concatenated into query text, (b) the IgnoreCase keyword rather than column collation, so all three vendors fold letter case identically and the PostgreSQL owner-search divergence is not repeated, (c) no caching of the request-keyed read, so caller input cannot grow an unbounded cache, and (d) URL-encoded link parameters in the template. Nothing about the change makes the application weaker than the security-principles.md baseline. Web controller rule: the controller branches on blank-versus-present to choose which repository call to make, which is request binding and delegation, not a business rule. The matching semantics live entirely in the derived query name. This is the same shape as OwnerController's blank-lastName normalization and does not extend the recorded controller-rule deviation. Note the deliberate divergence from that precedent: OwnerController strips its search term, while REQ-VET-003 does not strip the specialty, per the PRD's recorded narrowest reading and its open question. Blank means empty or all-whitespace and selects the unfiltered call; a padded non-blank name is passed through and matches nothing. Durable-memory writes made by this dispatch: new ADR docs/adr/2026-08-15-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-query.md; index rows in docs/adr/README.md for that ADR and for the non-goal ADR the product expert authored; docs/system-design.md gains a Caching subsection under Contracts, drops the Known Defects row saying the machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement, corrects the header provenance count from four confirmed defects to three, sets the Vets contract's Implements to REQ-VET-003, and rewrites open question 5's premise to separate cache invalidation from cache keying. Autofix audit: the handoff log carries no design-doc-autofix records, so nothing to audit. Deferred to doc-sync after implementation: the Implements column for VetRepository and VetController, which is left at REQ-VET-001 because the narrowing does not exist in the code yet.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain: NOT VERIFIED against the NVD in this review. No build file changed (build.gradle, settings.gradle, and gradle/ are absent from the change set), so this slice adds no dependency and clears the four checks in system-design.md § Adding a New Dependency vacuously. The OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle, and this reviewer has no network access, so no CVE match ran. Resolved framework floor for a human or CI to close out: Spring Boot 4.1.0, io.spring.dependency-management 1.1.7, GraalVM buildtools 1.1.2, CycloneDX 3.2.4.

Pre-existing, out of scope for this slice, recorded so it is not lost: `findAll(Pageable)` keeps @Cacheable("vets") while its Pageable is built from the caller-supplied `page` int, so an unauthenticated caller can already mint one entry per distinct page number in the same eviction-free cache the ADR reasons about. The diff neither introduces nor widens this (the `page` parameter and its caching predate the change), and docs/security-principles.md directs that pre-existing baseline absences are never findings. It is the adjacent instance of the class the ADR's option 2 explicitly deferred, so it belongs to whichever slice settles the `vets` eviction question.

`specialty` carries no length bound at the boundary. Reach is limited: it is a bound query parameter against a three-row seeded specialty table, and container URL/header limits cap it well below any allocation concern, so no attacker path is demonstrated. Worth a bound only if the vets surface ever gains authentication-free heavy queries.
approved_aspects: Data-access injection: the narrowing is a Spring Data derived query (VetRepository#findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, both overloads). The request-supplied name reaches the database as a bound JPQL parameter; no query text is concatenated anywhere in the change. The only @Query in the codebase (PetTypeRepository:36) is a static string untouched by this slice.

XSS / template-expression injection: the request-supplied `specialty` reaches the template only through `th:href="@{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}"`. Thymeleaf URL-encodes link parameters and HTML-escapes the attribute value; no th:utext or unescaped sink exists in vetList.html. The change additionally REMOVES five Thymeleaf preprocessing sites (`@{'/vets.html?page=__${...}__'}`) from the file it touches, replacing them with the link-expression parameter form. That is a net reduction in expression-evaluation surface on the exact page that now takes caller text — it closes the checklist's 'no request-supplied text in Thymeleaf preprocessing' item at the source rather than relying on `i` being numeric.

Cache poisoning / unbounded cache growth: the narrowed queries deliberately carry no @Cacheable, so an unauthenticated caller cannot mint cache entries in the eviction-free `vets` JCache. The controller routes blank input to the cached unfiltered read and non-blank input to the uncached narrowed read, so the cached key space stays application-controlled. Reasoning recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-15-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-query.md (options 1 and 2 rejected on exactly this ground) and repeated in the repository Javadoc.

Mass assignment: `specialty` binds as a scalar @RequestParam, not a field on a command object, so no new binder and no identifier-binding surface is introduced. No new @InitBinder or setDisallowedFields obligation arises.

Exposed surface: no new route. /vets.html and /vets each gain one optional query parameter with `defaultValue = ""`, so the pre-change request contract still resolves identically. No management endpoint, no mutating operation, no authentication assumption is touched.

Secrets: no token, password, key, credential, connection string, or URL literal appears anywhere in the diff, production or test. No new logging statement, so no new log sink for request-derived text.

Error handling and disclosure: neither controller path introduces a catch, a rethrow, or an exception message; a non-matching specialty yields an empty Page/Collection rather than an error, so no internal detail reaches the error page that renders exception messages.

Baseline comparison per docs/security-principles.md § Applying this section: the change introduces no row from the vulnerability-class table and leaves the application no weaker than the system-design.md Security Context baseline.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the veterinarian directory by specialty on both surfaces

blast_radius.note: Three production files in the single vet package plus its two test files and five docs; no build file, dependency, schema, config, or sensitive path touched, and the only reach beyond the slice's own surface is the shared pagination block in vetList.html.

semantic_surprise.note: The narrowing logic reads exactly as described and every branch traces cleanly, but rewriting the five paging hrefs from concatenated literals to link expressions with a named specialty parameter changes the unnarrowed directory's rendered links too - with the model attribute defaulting to the empty string those links now carry a trailing empty specialty=, which is behaviorally inert (defaultValue plus hasText both treat it as absent) yet is a rendered-output change on the pre-existing REQ-VET-001 surface that only a loose containsString assertion covers; separately, vetList.html now uses the name specialty for both the model attribute and the th:each variable in the vet-row loop, harmless today because the scopes do not overlap but a trap for the next edit.

test_adequacy.note: The matching semantics that actually carry the requirement are proven against a real H2 repository with real seeded data - whole-name match, case folding, partial-name rejection, unstripped padding, and paged totals over the join - and the controller tests pin the URL-encoded paging href verbatim, so a trimming, prefix-matching, or narrowing-dropping implementation would fail rather than pass.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved and the round-2 roster silence for security is expected, but security's approval parks three recommendations: the supply-chain check is explicitly NOT VERIFIED against the NVD (no plugin, no network), and findAll(Pageable) still caches on a caller-supplied page int in the same eviction-free vets cache the new ADR reasons about - pre-existing and correctly out of scope, but adjacent and unowned; test-reviewer likewise parked the missing JSON-surface unheld-specialty case, and doc-reviewer had to supersede its own line-21 record for pairing an autofix finding with an approved verdict.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the owner's recorded request point for point, including the deliberate revival of the /vets JSON surface under a fresh id, and the single design revision was bookkeeping to cover two doc paths for the autofix audit rather than a design change; the one unspecified case, blank space around a non-blank name, took the narrowest reading and was recorded as an open question instead of decided.

rationale: Logic is exactly as advertised and boundary-tested against real H2, so read fast but eyeball two things: the unnarrowed paging links now render a trailing empty specialty= that no test pins, and security's approval parks an unverified supply-chain check plus the adjacent eviction-free vets cache.
